answer: Reachability is the price of permanence: every seat must answer randomized liveness probes from a rotating sample of other seats, widening with the registry. With N seats the network carries N-squared obligations per epoch, so each clone drags the mesh's traffic onto itself. Missed probes draw graded fines, heaviest at the zenith of tenure. Each probe needs a fresh signature over a per-seat anchor tied to that epoch's ridge, so one host cannot answer for many seats. A lone agent absorbs a trickle; a farm of k pays far above k times it, since the mesh it must satisfy grew with it.
